classifications.rationale: The President presently makes the statutory import-impact finding that supports action under section 22; the legal determination occurs upon proclamation, although the predicted imports are conditional on section 104 expiring.
classifications.evidence: I find that in the event section 104 of the Defense Production Act of 1950, as amended, expires under its present terms

classifications.rationale: The President presently makes and declares the statutory necessity determination for the ensuing fees and quantitative limits; the determination occurs upon proclamation.
classifications.evidence: I find and declare that in the event section 104 of the Defense Production Act of 1950, as amended, expires under its present terms

classifications.rationale: The President begins a proclamation and supplies its effective date, but this fragment contains no object or consequence and is syntactically inseparable from the substantive provision in the next segment.
classifications.evidence: do hereby proclaim that on and after July 1, 1953

classifications.rationale: The President directly subjects listed imports to licensing, quantitative limits, and fees effective on the proclaimed date; agencies later administer these presently imposed legal restrictions.
classifications.evidence: articles included in the lists appended to and hereby made a part of this proclamation shall be subject to quantitative limitations and fees

classifications.rationale: The President presently makes a statutory representative-period determination, exempts federal imports, defines entry, and conditionally nullifies the proclamation; these legal consequences operate by the segment itself.
classifications.evidence: The provisions of this proclamation shall not apply to articles imported by or for the account of any department or agency of the Government of the United States.
